note: Each card shows how to send leads from one form tool to your lead address. A person who did not agree is still kept as a lead, but nobody is called or messaged until consent is asked.

templates.name: Google Ads lead form
steps: In Google Ads, open the lead form asset (or the lead form extension) of your campaign and choose 'Webhook integration' under 'Lead delivery option'.
Paste this address as the Webhook URL: {ADDRESS}
In the Key box type any word you like. Google sends it with every lead; we do not need it, because the secret address already protects this door.

Add one yes/no question to the form: the word 'consent' must be in its name, and its text is the sentence the person agrees to (for example: I agree that Sree Silks may call or WhatsApp me about my enquiry).
Press 'Send test data' in Google Ads. A test lead appears in your Leads within a minute. A person who did not agree is still kept as a lead, but we ask first before we call.

mapping.lead_id: external_id (the same lead sent twice is one lead)
mapping.a column with 'consent' in its id or nam: consent (its column_name is the wording the person saw)
mapping.lead_submit_time: consent_at (else the time we received it)

templates.consent: The form needs one yes/no question with 'consent' in its name. Google sends the question's own text as column_name (a deprecated field that may be missing): when it is missing the lead is kept but nobody is called until consent is asked.
verify: How a custom question appears in user_column_data (its column_id is not documented as CONSENT: check one real test lead and rename the question if needed).
Whether column_name is still sent (the documentation calls it deprecated).

templates.name: Typeform
steps: In your typeform open Connect, then Webhooks, then 'Add a webhook'.
Paste this address as the Destination URL: {ADDRESS}. It must start with https.
Add a Phone number question and an Email question. In the question's settings set its reference to 'phone' and 'email' (the reference is not shown to the person).
Add a Yes/No or Legal question whose reference is 'consent' and whose text is the sentence the person agrees to (for example: I agree that Sree Silks may call or WhatsApp me about my enquiry).
Switch the webhook on and press 'View deliveries', then 'Send test request'. A test lead appears in your Leads.

templates.name: Tally
steps: In Tally open your form, then Integrations, then Webhooks, then 'Connect'.
Paste this address as the Endpoint URL: {ADDRESS}
Add a Phone number question and an Email question (Tally sends their type, so no naming is needed).

Add a Checkboxes question with one option, the sentence the person agrees to (for example: I agree that Sree Silks may call or WhatsApp me about my enquiry). Put the word 'consent' in the question's label.
Press 'Test' in Tally. A test lead appears in your Leads. A form without the consent question still makes a lead; we ask before calling.

templates.name: Jotform
steps: In the Jotform Form Builder open Settings, then Integrations, search for Webhooks and click it.
Paste this address in the 'Add WebHook' box: {ADDRESS}/jotform . Jotform sends its answers as a multipart form, which this address (and only this one) reads.
Click 'Complete Integration', then 'Finish'.
In the form, give the phone field the unique name 'phone', the e-mail field 'email', the name field 'name' and the message field 'message' (Properties, then Advanced, then Unique Name).

Add a checkbox with one option, the sentence the person agrees to (for example: I agree that Sree Silks may call or WhatsApp me about my enquiry), and give it the unique name 'consent'. Submit the form once yourself: a lead appears in your Leads.

q7_consent: I agree that Sree Silks may call or WhatsApp me about my enquiry

mapping.q<number>_consent (a checkbox): consent (the ticked option's text is the wording the person saw; the time is when we received it)

templates.consent: One checkbox field whose unique name contains 'consent'. Jotform sends no time of its own that we know of, so the consent time is when we received the submission.
verify: Jotform's help page names only rawRequest; formID and submissionID are seen in third-party write-ups, not in Jotform's documentation.
How the Phone field's answer is shaped inside rawRequest (full, or area and phone): both are read.
How a checkbox answer is shaped in rawRequest (a list of the ticked options' text is assumed).

templates.name: LinkedIn Lead Gen Forms (through Zapier or Make)
steps: In Zapier make a Zap: trigger 'LinkedIn Lead Gen Forms', event 'New Lead Gen Form Response (Sponsored content)' (or Organic content for a company page). You need the Account Manager or Campaign Manager role on the ads account.
Action: 'Webhooks by Zapier', event 'POST', payload type 'Json'. URL: {ADDRESS}

Under Data add these names and pick the LinkedIn answer for each: name (first name and last name from LinkedIn, one after the other), phone, email, message (company and job title if you like), lead_id (the response's id).

Add consent = yes only if your LinkedIn form asks the person for permission; add consent_text = the exact sentence the person saw on the form; add consent_at = the time of the response from the trigger.
In Make the same recipe is: module 'LinkedIn Lead Gen Forms' then module 'HTTP, Make a request' (POST, body type Raw, content type JSON). Test the Zap with a test lead.

templates.consent: LinkedIn's own form has its consent and privacy text. Copy the exact sentence into consent_text and send consent=yes only for responses that agreed. Without them the lead is kept and we ask before calling.
verify: Zapier does not publish the output field names of the LinkedIn Lead Gen Forms trigger: choose them in the Zap editor with a real test lead.
Whether the trigger gives a 'consent' answer for the form's legal checkbox, and the response's time.

templates.name: Webflow forms
steps: In Webflow open Site settings, then Apps and integrations, then Webhooks, then 'Add webhook'. Trigger type: Form submission.
Paste this address as the Webhook URL: {ADDRESS}
Webhooks made in the dashboard cannot be signed; the secret address protects this door, so keep it private.

In the form give the fields the names Name, Phone, Email and Message. Add a checkbox whose name is the sentence the person agrees to and starts with the word Consent (for example: Consent: I agree that Sree Silks may call or WhatsApp me about my enquiry).
Publish the site and submit the form once yourself: a lead appears in your Leads.

mapping.payload.name: the form's name kept with the consent

templates.consent: One checkbox whose field name contains 'consent' and is the sentence itself (or a hidden field named consent_text with the sentence).
verify: Webflow's documentation does not say how a ticked checkbox appears in payload.data (true, on or yes are all read).
Which of payload.id and payload.formId identifies the submission (the documentation words both oddly).
Whether a Webflow form can hold a hidden input without custom code.

templates.name: TradeIndia lead e-mails
steps: In TradeIndia open your account settings and make sure inquiry e-mails go to one e-mail address you control.
Forward those e-mails to your Stack19 e-mail lead address (Lead sources, E-mail forwarding), or set that address as the inquiry e-mail.
Each e-mail is read by its 'Label: value' lines (buyer name, mobile, e-mail, city, product requirement). An e-mail without a number or an address is kept in the unparsed list for you to read.
TradeIndia hides some buyer contact details behind its own login: such an e-mail has no number and stays in the unparsed list.
